samples.summary: New tab-id guard is a 3-key denylist that misses the keys that are actually truthy on a live Yorkie proxy (`toString`/`toJSON`/`toJS`/`toJSForTest`/`getID`), so `PUT|GET .../tabs/toString/images` still walks past the `!worksheet` check
samples.evidence:
`UNSAFE_TAB_IDS = new Set(['__proto__','prototype','constructor'])` (line 51) is the only filter before the truthiness check at line 84 (`const worksheet = root.sheets?.[tabId]; if (!worksheet) throw ...`).

The sibling controller documents the exact bypass this misses — packages/backend/src/api/v1/worksheet-structure.controller.ts:84-90: "`root.sheets` is a Yorkie `JSONObject` proxy whose get trap answers `getID` / `toJSON` / `toJS` / `toJSForTest` / `toString` with a **function** — truthy — so `.../tabs/toString/insert` walked past a bare `if (!worksheet)` and handed the engine a function to splice `rowOrder` on. (`__proto__` is safe through that proxy only by accident...)". In production `root` is always a Yorkie proxy (yorkie.service.ts:36-57 attaches a real `yorkie.Document`), so the new denylist closes only the plain-object/unit-test case and leaves the *live-document* case open.

Attack: an authenticated workspace member sends `PUT /api/v1/workspaces/:ws/documents/:doc/tabs/toJSON/images`. `assertPlainTabId` passes, `root.sheets['toJSON']` returns the trap function (truthy), the guard passes, and `ws.images = {}` / `ws.images[id] = image` (lines 138-139) execute against that function object. The route answers 200 `{images}` for a write that was never persisted, and attacker-controlled data is attached to a live JS function object; `GET .../tabs/toJSON/images` reads it back, which is process-global rather than document-scoped state (a cross-workspace channel, since no workspace check reaches that object).

The denylist also under-covers the plain-object threat it claims to close: `({}).valueOf`, `.hasOwnProperty`, `.isPrototypeOf`, `.toLocaleString`, `.propertyIsEnumerable`, `.__defineGetter__` are all truthy inherited lookups, and `({}).prototype` is *undefined* (so one of the three listed keys is inert while several real ones are absent).

The repo already exports the correct both-sides-safe membership test — `safeWorksheetRecordKeys(sheets).includes(tabId)` (packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-record.ts:33, used at worksheet-structure.controller.ts:109) — which rejects every non-key, proxy or plain, instead of enumerating bad names.

samples.summary: The same `:tabId` truthiness guard is unfixed in every other worksheet tab controller; the images-controller guard makes the class read as handled while these routes still write through a prototype/proxy key
samples.evidence:
`worksheetOrThrow` in worksheet-rules.controller.ts:55-62 is byte-identical to the pre-fix images version (`const worksheet = root.sheets?.[tabId]; if (!worksheet) throw new NotFoundException(...)`) and line 99 writes straight through it: `this.worksheetOrThrow(root, tabId).conditionalFormats = rules;` with `rules` fully attacker-supplied.

Same unguarded shape at: worksheet-styles.controller.ts:55 (write at :94 `.rangeStyles = rangeStyles`), worksheet-dimensions.controller.ts:58 (writes at :136/:181/:226/:271), worksheet-charts.controller.ts:50 (write at :106), worksheet-filter-pivot.controller.ts:48 (:90/:136), worksheet.controller.ts:48 (:85/:131/:178), cells.controller.ts:89/:126/:159/:194/:231.

Vector, per the proxy behaviour documented at worksheet-structure.controller.ts:84-90: `PUT /api/v1/workspaces/:ws/documents/:doc/tabs/toString/conditional-formats` passes the guard (the trap returns a truthy function) and assigns caller-controlled `rules` onto that object, answering 200 for a write that never lands. On any plain-object root, `sheets['__proto__']` is `Object.prototype` and the same line writes `Object.prototype.conditionalFormats` — process-wide prototype pollution, which is precisely the failure the images controller just added a guard for. Only worksheet-structure.controller.ts uses the correct `safeWorksheetRecordKeys(...).includes(tabId)` check; the fix should be that helper applied uniformly, not a per-controller denylist.

samples.summary: The write key one line below the new guard — `image.id` straight from the request body — is still unvalidated for prototype keys
samples.evidence:
Line 139: `for (const image of images) ws.images[image.id] = image;`. `parseImages`/`parseImage` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/worksheet-images.ts:54, `id: requireString(i.id, 'id')`) accepts any non-empty string, including `__proto__`, `constructor` and `toString`. The delta hardens the `:tabId` key against exactly these names but leaves the adjacent, equally caller-controlled `images[].id` key open.

On the plain-object path `ws.images['__proto__'] = image` reassigns the prototype of the freshly created images object (assignment invokes the `Object.prototype.__proto__` setter, not a data write); through the Yorkie proxy it persists a CRDT key named `__proto__` inside `sheets[tab].images`, which every later consumer that materializes that map by assignment (clone/copy/migration loops such as worksheet-shape-migration.ts:475) then replays as a prototype write. Validating the id with the same rule as the tab id (or rejecting non-`[A-Za-z0-9_-]` ids) makes the two keys consistent.

samples.summary: New chart-copy loop in `duplicateTab` assigns into a fresh object using a key taken from a CRDT-derived snapshot, so a chart stored under `__proto__` reassigns the copy's prototype
samples.evidence: Lines 185-193 build `const charts: NonNullable<Worksheet['charts']> = {}` and then `charts[chartId] = ...` for every `Object.entries(copy.charts)` pair. `worksheet` is an `unwrapJson` snapshot (see the docblock at tab-ops.ts:141-146 and yorkie-json.ts:22-33, which ends in `JSON.parse`), and `JSON.parse` yields `__proto__` as an *own* enumerable property, so `Object.entries` will surface it. A collaborator who writes a chart under the key `__proto__` directly through the Yorkie client (the frontend talks to the Yorkie server, so CRDT keys are not gated by these API validators) makes `charts['__proto__'] = chart` run the prototype setter instead of storing a chart: the duplicated tab silently loses that chart and the object handed to `root.sheets[newTabId].charts` has an attacker-chosen prototype. `Object.defineProperty`/`Object.create(null)`/a key skip-list would avoid it. Low confidence: I did not confirm the Yorkie set trap permits storing a `__proto__` key in the first place.

samples.summary: `withSref` now copies both axis arrays per thread, making GET /comments O(threads x axis length) in allocations — a cheap request-amplification lever on a large sheet
samples.evidence: Lines 717-718 changed from passing `worksheet.rowOrder`/`colOrder` by reference to `Array.from(...)`, and `withSref` is invoked once per thread inside the tab walk (comments.controller.ts:240 `out.push(withSref(thread, worksheet))`). Each thread therefore materializes both full axes. Axes reach 10,000 entries per API call (`MaxAxisEntries`, packages/backend/src/yorkie/worksheet-structure.ts:56) and far more through the editor, so a workspace member with a sheet carrying a few thousand threads turns one authenticated `GET .../comments` (`syncMode: 'readonly'`, so no write cost to repeat) into tens of millions of element copies — an availability amplification introduced by this delta. Hoisting the two `Array.from` calls out of the per-thread loop (one detach per worksheet) removes it without changing behaviour.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. worksheet-images.controller.ts:51 defines UNSAFE_TAB_IDS as exactly the three keys quoted, and assertPlainTabId (53-55) is the only filter before the truthiness check at 83-84; it is the sole gate on both PUT (via worksheetOrThrow at 82, called at 133/135) and GET (95). The repo itself documents the missed vector: worksheet-structure.controller.ts:84-90 states root.sheets is a Yorkie JSONObject proxy whose get trap answers getID/toJSON/toJS/toJSForTest/toString with a truthy function that walked past a bare `if (!worksheet)`, and worksheet-structure-axis.controller.spec.ts:234-251 is a live regression test requiring NotFoundException for those five proxy keys plus __proto__/constructor — none of the five proxy keys are in the images controller's denylist. Production uses a real proxy: yorkie.service.ts:42-57 constructs and attaches a genuine yorkie.Document, so doc.getRoot() in this controller is the proxy, meaning the denylist closes only the plain-object case. No compensating guard exists: the correct both-sides-safe membership test safeWorksheetRecordKeys (packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-record.ts:33) is used by worksheet-structure.controller.ts:109 but is not imported by the images controller, and main.ts:66's ValidationPipe validates DTO bodies, not the raw URL-decoded :tabId path param. This is unvalidated attacker-controlled input used as an object key (unsafe input handling / prototype-pollution-adjacent), in-lane and blocking; the write at 138-139 lands on a non-worksheet object while the route returns 200.

mergedFrom.summary: `tabId` route param is used as an unfiltered object key for both the existence check and the write, giving a prototype-pollution shape (`PUT .../tabs/__proto__/images`)

finding.summary: User-controlled `:tabId` is used directly as an object key and then written into (`ws.images = {}`), so a request with `tabId=__proto__` can reach an assignment onto `Object.prototype` if the root ever behaves like a plain object
finding.evidence: `setImages` takes `:tabId` straight from the URL (Express URL-decodes, so `%5F%5Fproto%5F%5F` → `__proto__`) and does `root.sheets?.[tabId]` in `worksheetOrThrow` (line 51-57). On a plain JS object `sheets['__proto__']` returns `Object.prototype` — truthy — so the NotFound guard passes and `doc.update` then executes `ws.images = {}` followed by `ws.images[image.id] = image` (lines 97-98), writing attacker-controlled data onto `Object.prototype`. Against a real Yorkie object proxy the outcome depends on the SDK's `get` trap (the SDK is not installed in this tree, so I could not confirm which way it falls); the controller's own spec harness uses a plain object, which is the shape where this is exploitable. Note the identical pattern already exists pre-change in `worksheet-charts.controller.ts:106-110`, so this is a new instance of an existing pattern rather than a new class. A cheap fix is to reject any `tabId` that is not present in `root.tabOrder`, or to use `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(sheets, tabId)`.

verdict.reason: The finding claims `worksheet-images.controller.ts` uses `:tabId` as an object key with no sanitization, letting `tabId=__proto__` reach `ws.images = {}` on `Object.prototype`. The file in this tree contains exactly that guard. `UNSAFE_TAB_IDS = new Set(['__proto__','prototype','constructor'])` and `assertPlainTabId()` are defined at worksheet-images.controller.ts:51-55 and throw `NotFoundException`. `worksheetOrThrow` calls `assertPlainTabId(tabId)` at line 82, before the `root.sheets?.[tabId]` lookup at line 83, so both `worksheetOrThrow` invocations on the PUT path (line 133 pre-check and line 135 inside `doc.update`) reject the prototype keys before the writes at lines 138-139. The GET path is guarded independently at line 95, before its read at line 99. `worksheetOrThrow` is private with no other callers (grep for `assertPlainTabId|UNSAFE_TAB_IDS` returns only this file), so there is no unguarded entry point to the protected write. The vector is also regression-tested at worksheet-images.controller.spec.ts:98-112, which drives `setImages` with `__proto__`, `constructor`, `prototype`, expects `NotFoundException`, and asserts `Object.prototype` has no `images` property. The reviewer's cited lines 51-57 are the guard itself, so the quoted evidence describes code that is not present as described. The reviewer's own proposed fix is already implemented in equivalent form; the file comment at lines 43-46 documents why a deny-list was chosen over `hasOwnProperty` (a Yorkie proxy traps `get`, not `getOwnPropertyDescriptor`). The unguarded sibling pattern in worksheet-charts.controller.ts:49-50 and 106-110 is real but was explicitly scoped out by this finding as a pre-existing note and is a different location.
